prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Finish hint changes have shown no clear effect across 2 tests.
Evidence is still thin for sign_in reorder changes as only one test has been completed.
Evidence is still thin for home redesign changes as only one test has been completed.
Evidence is still thin for adoption redesign, choose_path copy, and home new_flow changes with only one test completed each.
Predictions were consistently too high across all round 1 tests.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: +1.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, copy: +2.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, hint: -1.8% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- home, new_flow: +2.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, redesign: -2.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

- sign_in: 76.0%, median 3s / mean 567s

Changes:
0: [choose_path, redesign] Choose path grid layout redesign: Redesign the choose path screen with a structured grid layout and prominent visual cards comparing pre-made pets and custom creation. (why: The choose_path step has a long mean duration of 514s despite low median (8s), showing that undecided users stall on plain text option links.)
1: [adoption, new_screen] Pet traits customization screen: Insert a new pet personality traits step before adoption certificate confirmation to build deeper emotional investment. (why: Adoption stage has the lowest completion rate (60.9%) and 1017s mean duration; early personal engagement improves completion.)
2: [adoption, redesign] Spotlight layout pick friend screen: Redesign the pet selection screen with a spotlight hero layout featuring high-definition companion previews. (why: The adoption drop-off (60.9%) indicates users need a more engaging and clear view of available pets before committing.)
3: [home, new_flow] Estimated time rendering progress flow: Transform the waiting screen into a dynamic generation status flow with active time estimates and progress indicators. (why: The home waiting step takes a median of 201s and mean of 2336s, leading to abandonment without continuous feedback.)
4: [sign_in, copy] Existing account recovery sign-in headline: Update sign-in headline to emphasize logging in to restore previously saved desktop pets and account data. (why: 8 support emails reported pets missing or reset after signing in, indicating confusion around account linking versus creating new profiles.)
5: [home, layout] Centered layout pet generation status: Switch waiting screen to a centered layout featuring an animated progress bar component. (why: High waiting screen mean duration (2336s) requires explicit visual focus so users know background processing is active.)
6: [finish, hint] Desktop tray display hint: Add explicit hint text on the home intro screen detailing how to locate the pet icon in the desktop system tray. (why: 3 support emails specifically noted pets not appearing on the desktop or failing to display after completing setup.)
7: [home, wait_info] Desktop preparation wait notification request: Enable notification opt-in controls on the waiting screen so users can minimize the app while generation finishes. (why: Long rendering wait times (mean 2336s) cause users to close the app; desktop notifications allow safe multitasking.)
